page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with a heading at the top and a verse quotation inside the text. One marginal note in the left margin, beside the paragraph about the best trout. Running head at the top right. Page number at the top left.

main_text.head: Detrutta, aurata & variola.
main_text.p: NEC tu, trutta, filentio damnanda adeo in menfarum aulicarum gloria prealiis nobilitata, faporeq, fuavi celebrata, ut etiam Aufonius in fua Mofella te non conticuerit, fic canens,
Teque inter geminas fpecies, neutrumq; & vtrumque, Qui necdum Salamo, nec tam Salarambiguufque Amborum medio fario intercepte fub zuo

Ex quibus verfibus colligitur, farionem, variolam feu forellam, falarem & falmonem eundem effe pifcem, dicit, falarem forellam adhuc teneram, farionem media ætatis, jam vero grandem forellam Salmonem, feu truttam Salmoneam, cujusmodi plurimi Germania amnes, rivi, rivuli, torrentes, fertilissimi [?] funt. Celebrantur in primis, quae in fluminibus fontium abundantibus capiuntur. Porro elixae affis praeflant, eduntur ex aceto, rarius friguntur, nec alia condimenta patiuntur, fuo enim fapore fatis placent.

Sale quoq; condiuntur, laquearibus Quænam forellæ optimæ? adium appenfa afservantur. Caeterum nobiliores femper habentur & pretiofiores, purpureis aureisq; maculis variegatæ, & quibus caro rubescens, & dura est: candida, & quibus est caro al-

page.notes: Several words in the lower half of the page are faint and show-through from the reverse side; those readings are doubtful and marked [?]. The verse quotation (Ausonius, Mosella) is copied from the print as I see it, not from memory. The running head and page number are read from a small, faint print at the top and may be inexact. The left margin note is read as "Quænam forellæ optimæ?". The ghost marks at the foot of the scan are show-through and are left out. The final line "ro al-" continues the paragraph and is not a catchword.
